title: Global constructible immersed refinement factoring through local strata
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme (def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions). Given a finite affine open cover W indexed by Fin n and, for each chart W_a, a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification T_a (def-constructible-stratification), there exists a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification S of X such that each stratum immersion of S factors by an actual scheme morphism through one local stratum immersion T_a,b -> W_a -> X. No morphism U -> X or finite-etale property is assumed.

proof.text: Extend each local partition by the closed complement of its affine chart. Affine charts are quasi-compact and hence retrocompact; local constructible subsets are constructible in X. Realize the complement as a closed subscheme and compose local immersions with the chart inclusion.

Take the finite common refinement of these extended partitions using intersections, represented by fibre products. Discard empty parts. For each nonempty part choose a point and a chart containing it; refinement puts the entire part into one local stratum of that chart. The empty base admits the zero-stratum partition.

Replace each chosen refined scheme by its fibre product with the local representative. The composite immersion has the same image, so the finite partition and constructibility persist. The second projection gives the actual factorization through the local representative.

theorem exists_global_stratification_factoring_local
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (n : ℕ) (W : Fin n → X.Opens)
    (hW : ∀ a, IsAffineOpen (W a))
    (hcover : (⋃ a : Fin n, (W a : Set X)) = Set.univ)
    (T : ∀ a, LocallyClosedStratification (W a))
    (hc : ∀ a b, Topology.IsConstructible ((T a).stratum b)) :
    ∃ S : LocallyClosedStratification X,
      (∀ i, Topology.IsConstructible (S.stratum i)) ∧
      ∀ i, ∃ (a : Fin n) (b : Fin (T a).n)
        (q : S.domain i ⟶ (T a).domain b),
        q ≫ ((T a).immersion b ≫ (W a).ι) = S.immersion i
